method: Side-by-side comparison of each inherited prompt and solution with the complete parent on the cited physical/PDF page of the SHA-256-pinned Cambridge examination PDF.

retained_components: tensorial difference of two symmetric connections
projectively equivalent connection form and trace for the covector
missing_or_changed_components: definition of a linear connection
existence, uniqueness, and coefficient derivation for the Levi-Civita connection
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The inherited prompt starts at the third stage of the examination question and omits the definition and full metric-connection derivation that motivate the final projective-equivalence result.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution addresses only the retained difference-tensor and projective pieces, gives polarization as an assertion, and cannot cover the omitted first half of the complete parent.

retained_components: coordinate exterior derivative, nilpotence, pullback naturality, and Lie-derivative commutation
conformal Killing coefficient and Maxwell symmetry conclusion
missing_or_changed_components: proof that the coordinate definition is chart independent
the mixed volume tensor calculation and all supplied epsilon-contraction identities
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The synopsis names the beginning and end results but compresses the central tensor calculation, removes the supplied identities, and does not retain the requested chart-independence proof as an explicit task.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution replaces the required mixed-volume-tensor derivation by an unproved statement that the Hodge star is conformally invariant, so it does not solve the complete source parent by the requested route.

retained_components: Riemann algebraic symmetries and both Bianchi identities
vector and covector Ricci commutators and twice-contracted derivative identity
missing_or_changed_components: explicit derivation from the examination's front-page curvature convention
full indexed cancellation proving the final derivative identity
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The prompt lists most target statements but drops the source convention dependency and turns a staged derivation into a broad checklist without preserving the precise index placements needed for a sign audit.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution repeatedly says identities follow or terms cancel without displaying the source-requested derivations, and its last paragraph does not establish the nontrivial final contraction calculation.

retained_components: Riemann definition, Bianchi identities, vacuum curvature wave equation, and linearized conclusion
gauge-invariance question on a flat background
missing_or_changed_components: the source's exact nonlinear identity and determination of its coefficient alpha by symmetry
the dimension-general setup, normal-coordinate allowance, and full contracted Bianchi task
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The inherited version substitutes a schematic wave equation for the exact supplied identity and eliminates the coefficient-finding subproblem, so a connected, graded stage of the parent has disappeared.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution never determines alpha and summarizes all commutator terms as producing the displayed equation; it therefore cannot verify either the exact nonlinear identity or every requested source subpart.

retained_components: linearized point-mass metric and equatorial null-orbit equation
circular photon orbit, instability, and approximation warning
missing_or_changed_components: the source definitions and interpretations of both conserved quantities
all formulas or conventions taken from the examination's optional lecture handout
comparisons.prompt_assessment: Although the main orbit result survives, the adaptation does not supply the handout material on which the source permits reliance and omits the explicit conserved-quantity interpretation requested in the complete parent.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution asserts that the metric and orbit equation follow, without deriving them from the point source or showing the conserved first integrals, leaving most of the complete calculation unwritten.

retained_components: slowly rotating thin shell and qualitative linear interior gravitomagnetic field
constant interior dragging rate and Lense-Thirring interpretation
missing_or_changed_components: the exact source density, four-velocity, metric ansatz, and requested values of A, B_alpha, and C
the supplied l=1 Laplacian hint and explicit interior timelike-geodesic analysis
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The inherited prompt reduces a fully specified field-equation problem to a qualitative solve request and a final rate, removing source data, named intermediate fields, and the retained mathematical hint.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution invokes matching to an exterior dipole without carrying out the source integral, boundary matching, metric reconstruction, or requested geodesic calculation, so it is not independently checkable.

retained_components: stress-conservation moment identity and far-zone quadrupole scaling
weak-source compactness estimate
missing_or_changed_components: the printed tensor-mode equation, retarded-potential solution, far-zone integral, and trace-free stress definition
a complete derivation in the examination's field variables rather than a substituted TT-projector formula
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The adaptation keeps the familiar quadrupole destination but discards the source's supplied starting equations and replaces its field variable and requested derivation with a different compact TT presentation.
comparisons.solution_assessment: Only the moment identity and dimensional estimate are sketched; the retarded integral, source definitions, projection, numerical factors, and full chain to the source's quadrupole field are absent.

retained_components: linearized wave-gauge equations and residual gauge condition
null plane-wave packet and two transverse-traceless polarizations
missing_or_changed_components: the supplied exact Ricci formula, wave-coordinate condition, decay hypothesis, and explicit two-stage gauge hint
the source's detailed conditions on k and every component function H_mu_nu
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The main outline remains recognizable, but necessary supplied formulas and the constructive residual-gauge hint are removed while the precise plane-wave conditions are compressed into a generic reduction request.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution states that residual transformations remove components and trace but does not construct the two gauge transformations, determine their coefficient, or verify the full component conditions requested in part c.

retained_components: static Killing-flow hydrostatic relation
radiation equation of state, integrated density law, and no-free-surface conclusion
missing_or_changed_components: the initial derivation of the relativistic Euler equation from stress-energy conservation
the source's two explicit hydrostatic-equilibrium hypotheses and complete normalization derivation
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The prompt begins after one connected derivation and presents the central pressure law as the first target, shortening the parent instead of preserving its conservation-to-equilibrium logical chain.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The projection and Killing acceleration are stated compactly, but the omitted general Euler stage is never solved and the stationarity assumptions are not checked in the detail required by the parent.

retained_components: a velocity-potential description of isentropic perfect-fluid stress and number conservation
relativistic Euler equation in modern signature
missing_or_changed_components: the source's constrained action with independent n and enthalpy, and its dp/dh variation
the complete evolution equations and the stated static weak-field slow-motion limit with interpretation
comparisons.prompt_assessment: This is not a convention-only adaptation: it replaces the source action by a different P(X) theory and deletes the entire Newtonian-limit half, so the source-parent architecture and connected tasks are materially changed.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution correctly varies the substituted P(X) action but necessarily does not solve the actual constrained variations, density and energy evolution, or linearized fluid equations requested by the cited parent.

retained_components: Lie derivative on several tensor types and its commutator identity
closure of Killing fields and commutation of stationary and axial symmetries
missing_or_changed_components: the source's explicit extension through a mixed (1,1) tensor and arbitrary tensors
the optional Jacobi-identity hint and a careful proof that asymptotic normalization fixes constant coefficients globally
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The prompt retains most headline requests but compresses the arbitrary-tensor construction and removes source scaffolding that is necessary to audit the final global symmetry argument as one complete parent.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The solution supplies two component formulas and then asserts the general extension, Jacobi consequence, and global coefficient conclusion; it is far shorter than a derivation of all requested stages.

retained_components: static anti-de Sitter metric, radial first integral, timelike return time, and null boundary time
affine versus coordinate-time distinction for outgoing null rays
missing_or_changed_components: the source's starting Cartesian anti-de Sitter metric and derivation of the polar form
the complete Christoffel-symbol calculation and proof that initially radial geodesics remain radial
comparisons.prompt_assessment: The inherited exercise starts from the result of part a and skips all of part b plus the first demand of part c, reducing a five-part complete parent to its radial dynamical tail.
comparisons.solution_assessment: The radial oscillator and null integrations are handled, but there is no Cartesian conversion, action-based Christoffel derivation, angular equation, or proof of preservation of radial motion.
